justification: SEPP auto-stale (regulatory-currency plan W3, founder decision 2026-07-29): a detected version change of a source instrument stamps stale_since/stale_reason on dependent standards rows. Founder-specified behaviour: values KEEP SERVING with a visible notice in every consumer (CDC screen warnings, secondary-dwelling row basis) - never a silent stale figure, never a blanked row. Cleared during re-verification.

pre_impl.existing_data: Seam verified live: legislation_monitor.check_instrument changed-block updates instrument_registry and the alert assembly lists changed instruments; instrument keys sepp_exempt_complying_2008 and sepp_housing_2021 confirmed in instrument_currency; consumers are load_cdc_standards and fetch_sepp_housing_standards/load_regulatory_configs feeding calc_feasibility. Migration 061 applied to prod (additive columns, verified).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The E&C Codes SEPP feeds BOTH tables - housing_sepp_standards carries rows citing SEPP (E&C) 2008 (e.g. secondary-dwelling max_floor_area) - so its mapping stamps both, while Housing 2021 stamps housing only. The calc_feasibility boundary re-validation would have silently dropped the stale fields (fresh dict build); _validate_sepp_sd_config and the boundary call now pass them through explicitly.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No behaviour change while stale_since IS NULL (all rows today). The monitor's changed-block gains one function call; loaders gain two columns; the engine and the SD row gain a conditional notice sentence. Granny-flat service staleness notice deferred as a follow-up (its endpoints only 503 on absent standards).

functions.name: mark_dependent_standards_stale
functions.input: db connection, changed instrument key and label, old and new version strings
functions.output: human-readable alert lines naming each stamped table and row count
functions.if_none: an instrument with no mapped standards table returns an empty list and touches nothing; WHERE stale_since IS NULL means the FIRST detected change dates the notice and repeats never overwrite it

functions.name: load_cdc_standards
functions.input: connection and code name; now also reads stale_since/stale_reason per row
functions.output: standards dict carrying the latest stale_since and first stale_reason across rows
functions.if_none: no stale rows leaves both keys None and the engine emits no notice - identical to pre-change behaviour

functions.name: _validate_sepp_sd_config
functions.input: min_lot_size row dict, now possibly carrying stale fields
functions.output: validated config dict with stale fields passed through when present
functions.if_none: absent stale fields are simply not added; validation semantics for values and zones are unchanged

values.value: stale_since/stale_reason stamped by the monitor on cdc_eligibility_standards and housing_sepp_standards
values.read_at: load_cdc_standards and fetch_sepp_housing_standards; rendered as a notice in CDC screen warnings and the secondary-dwelling row basis
values.if_missing: NULL means no notice anywhere - the exact behaviour before this change

queries.purpose: stamp dependent standards stale on an instrument version change
queries.where_clause: WHERE stale_since IS NULL - only not-yet-stale rows, so the first change wins and the notice date stays honest

break_it.scenario: A SEPP amendment lands and the standards keep rendering with no indication anything changed.
break_it.what_happens: The exact silent-staleness this workstream exists to kill - confident figures from a superseded instrument.
break_it.how: The monitor's changed-block stamps the mapped tables in the same transaction as the registry update; the engine and the SD row render the notice whenever stale_since is set. Pinned by tests at monitor, loader and both render sites.
break_it.repro: Set stale_since on the standards rows and run the CDC screen - the warning names the change and date.

break_it.scenario: The notice blanks or blocks the figures instead of annotating them.
break_it.what_happens: Violates the founder-specified behaviour - reports must keep showing the last-reviewed values.
break_it.how: Staleness never enters validation or the fail-closed paths; test_stale_standards_still_screen_with_notice asserts the screen RAN and test_stale_config_renders_value_with_note asserts 'Likely permissible' still renders.
break_it.repro: Run calc_feasibility with a stale config - the answer is unchanged, only the basis gains the note.

break_it.scenario: Repeated monitor runs after the same amendment keep re-stamping and the notice date drifts forward.
break_it.what_happens: The notice would always claim the change was 'detected today', hiding how long re-verification has been pending.
break_it.how: WHERE stale_since IS NULL makes the first stamp permanent until cleared by re-verification; pinned by test asserting the clause on every UPDATE.
break_it.repro: Run mark_dependent_standards_stale twice - the second run matches zero rows.

break_it.scenario: A boundary re-validation drops the stale fields and the PDF path renders values with no notice while the workbench shows one.
break_it.what_happens: Inconsistent surfaces - the paid document is the one missing the caveat.
break_it.how: _validate_sepp_sd_config and calc_feasibility's boundary dict pass stale fields through explicitly; the SD-row test exercises the full injected-config path.
break_it.repro: calc_feasibility with a stale sepp_standards dict - the granny-flat basis carries the note.

post_merge.db_reset: Migration 061 already applied to prod (additive columns, verified via information_schema). All rows NULL, so nothing renders differently until the monitor first detects a change.
post_merge.other_repo: None. Fly legislation-monitor picks the code up on its next manual deploy (fly deploy -a plotdetect-legislation-monitor - auto-deploy is not wired for Fly). Follow-up: granny-flat service staleness notice; re-verification runbook is documented in the migration header.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - simulate: UPDATE housing_sepp_standards SET stale_since=now(), stale_reason='test' WHERE development_type='secondary_dwelling'; generate a report - the granny-flat row shows the note with the value intact; then clear the stamp and the note disappears.
